lead.question: For every n≥0 count the rooted oriented nearest-neighbor simple closed walks of length 2n with root (0,0) in {−1,0,1}×Z. Empty walk once, no out-and-back of length two. Prove the formal generating-function identity with numerator 1−4x+14x²−24x³+37x⁴−36x⁵+16x⁶−12x⁷ and denominator (1+x²)²(1−2x)².
lead.title: A022444: Number of self-avoiding closed walks (from (0,0) to (0,0)) of length 2n in strip {-1, 0, 1} X Z.
lead.decisive_test: Generate polygons up to horizontal translation with a 3-tip cut, weight each edge by z, and mark every visited middle-rail vertex w. The derivative at w=1 counts which vertex is translated onto the origin. Multiply nonempty counts by 2 for orientation, add the empty walk, substitute x=z² and verify a rational identity. A022445 (outer rail) should use the same transfer with a different marked rail, not a separate discovery.
lead.blocker: Read Jacques Labelle, Self-avoiding walks and polyominoes in strips (Bull. ICA 23, 1998), and Michael von Thaden’s 2026 three-row polygon enumeration before claims of novelty. The distinction is a specified starting rail rather than unrooted polygons up to translation. Confirm whether a prior paper already supplies the marking.

review.statement: For every integer n ≥ 0, let a(n) count ordered nearest-neighbor walks v₀,…,v₂ₙ in {−1,0,1} × ℤ with v₀ = v₂ₙ = (0,0). For n ≥ 2 require v₀,…,v₂ₙ₋₁ to be pairwise distinct. Set a(0) = 1 and a(1) = 0. The claim in ℤ[[x]] is Σₙ a(n)xⁿ = (1−4x+14x²−24x³+37x⁴−36x⁵+16x⁶−12x⁷)/((1+x²)²(1−2x)²).
review.significance: A polygon of fixed perimeter can visit the middle rail a variable number of times. That number determines how many translations put a vertex at the prescribed root. Marking it gives a candidate proof of the exact rooted identity. Priority remains unresolved.
review.settlement_test: A bijection that preserves perimeter and the number of possible middle-rail roots, followed by a formal generating-function calculation, proves the claim for every n. One rigorously enumerated coefficient that disagrees would refute it. A prior source proving the marked count or an explicitly equivalent identity would establish prior resolution.
review.aliases: OEIS A022444, middle-rail-rooted self-avoiding polygons on the three-row square-lattice strip, or rooted oriented polygons on ℤ × {0,1,2} with root (0,1). A022445 specifies an outer-rail root and is a companion problem.
review.attempt:
Jacques Labelle authored A022444. Its entry labels the rational function conjectural and credits Sean A. Irvine with extending the coefficients in 2019. Ralf Stephan is credited with the companion outer-rail conjecture in 2004. [A022444](https://oeis.org/A022444) · [A022445](https://oeis.org/A022445)

Michael von Thaden’s July 2026 v1 gives perimeter counts and refinements by the vertical steps in the two end columns. Those statistics alone do not specify the number of middle-rail vertices. I found no verified earlier proof of the exact rooted formula. Labelle’s 1998 paper remains the material priority check. [von Thaden](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27397v1) · [Labelle’s author copy](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/264931833_Self-avoiding_walks_and_polyominoes_in_strips)
review.proof_or_witness:
Rotate the strip so its three rails run horizontally. Translate each nonempty unoriented polygon until its leftmost column is 0. Every cut between successive columns of its span crosses exactly two polygon edges. The crossing count is positive by connectedness, even because a cycle enters and leaves each side equally often, and at most three. Give every edge weight z and every visited middle-rail vertex weight w. Write x = z².

At a cut, record the occupied pair of rails. Type A is an adjacent pair, with two possible positions. Type B is the pair of outer rails. At either end the two tips must be connected by the unique vertical interval, of weight zw for A or z²w for B. Both intervals visit the middle rail once.

At an interior column, unchanged tips go straight. A change between A and B keeps their common outer tip straight and moves the other tip by one vertical edge. A direct change between the two distinct A positions is impossible because their common middle tip already has degree two and the required vertical connection would pass through it. These exhaust the possibilities by degree two at each occupied vertex. Conversely, the transitions extend two disjoint strands, and the two end intervals join them into one simple cycle. Thus each allowed sequence, with its actual adjacent-pair positions specified, reconstructs exactly one translation class.

Charge the initial cut x for its two horizontal edges. Each subsequent transition pays x for the next cut and marks the middle vertex of the intervening column if visited. In state order (A,B), with rows incoming and columns outgoing, the matrix is T = [[xw, xzw], [2xzw, x]]. The factor 2 counts the two choices when leaving B for A. With initial row u = (2zw,z²w) and terminal column v = (zw,z²w)ᵀ, the polygon series is P = x u(I−T)⁻¹v. The constant matrix of T vanishes, so the inverse sums all finite transition sequences, including zero transitions for a one-cut polygon. Inverting gives P(x,w) = xw²(2x−x²+3x³w)/((1−xw)(1−x)−2x³w²).

Choosing a middle-rail vertex specifies the unique horizontal translation sending it to the root. Each resulting cycle has two traversal directions. Hence the required series is 1 + 2∂P/∂w evaluated at w=1. For an explicit algebra check, put b = 2x−x²+3x³, d = (1−x)²−2x³ = (1−2x)(1+x²), and h = x(1−x)+4x³. The rooted numerator over d² is d² + 2x[(2b+3x³)d+bh]. Expansion gives 1−4x+14x²−24x³+37x⁴−36x⁵+16x⁶−12x⁷, as claimed. For A022445 the same cut construction marks a specified outer rail, retaining the two adjacent-pair positions as distinct states.
review.remaining_obligation: An independent checker can audit the column bijection and root multiplicity directly from the proof. I checked the final polynomial identity in an isolated JavaScript calculation at ten distinct integers, sufficient since its degree is at most seven. A dedicated notebook interface was unavailable. The catalogue page and both attempted agent.txt routes were inaccessible, so I used the supplied brief and the original OEIS statement. I located Labelle’s eleven-page scan but could not verify its contents from the available rendering. Checking pages 88–98 for an equivalent rooted enumeration remains necessary before assigning priority or novelty. This is an intake draft with no automatic solution credit.
